numbering.explanation: Scroll the named options with up/down and select with tick. Appendix C’s section numerals are not established as keypad shortcuts. Two-digit shortcuts are explicitly documented within zone and output Type selectors.

examples.meaning: Final Exit within zone Type; not a root menu.
Open/Close within output Type. The same value means 24 Hour Alarm in zone Type.
Logical zone and panel input notation; not levels in a menu address.

caveats: A/B/C/D are programmable setting keys, not universal menu addresses.
Partitioned and part-setting systems show alternative branches.
Numbers in device, user, zone, event and output selectors identify records.
The order field arranges source entries; it is not a numeric shortcut.
Repeated selector templates represent installation-specific records, not a claimed fixed population.
Body-only entries and introductory value catalogues are marked where the exact LCD scroll position is not established.

navigation.action: Scroll options; tick selects; cross returns one level.
Cross up to Leave installer mode?, then tick confirms. This v6 guide requires exit faults to be rectified.
Normally commits configuration changes. Factory default and documented radio-deletion behavior are exceptions, not covered by a universal save rule.
The two-digit zone/output function shortcut is context-specific and not displayed as a menu address.
Context-dependent toggles, zone-name/address display or field actions; do not assume right always means Enter.
Switch between all zones and remaining untested zones; tick ends the test.
Older/newer events; right shows extra information.
Toggle I/O and confirm the change.

gaps.title: Exact panel and software baseline
gaps.question: What model and firmware version does About→Panel show on the i-on panel you want FINDR to match?
gaps.reason: The installer reference covers 6.0.xx and the official user/admin source covers 7.02.xx. They cannot be treated as one installed firmware.
gaps.neededEvidence: Photograph of About→Panel showing model, firmware and system mode; exclude any access codes.

gaps.title: Conditional menu visibility
gaps.question: Is the target i-on40H+ configured for partitions or part-setting, and which expanders, radio keypads and communications modules are fitted?
gaps.reason: The source explicitly hides branches according to mode and discovered hardware.
gaps.neededEvidence: About screens or an installed-device list plus the relevant menu photographs.

gaps.title: Local keypad setup is a different menu
gaps.question: Which exact keypad model and keypad firmware do you use—KEY-KP01, KEY-KPZ01, KEY-FKPZ or another model?
gaps.reason: This atlas covers panel menus. Keypad-local contrast, illumination and buzzer settings require the exact keypad installation guide and firmware.
gaps.neededEvidence: Keypad model label and firmware screen; the model’s local setup instructions if available.

gaps.title: Radio detector deletion wording conflicts
gaps.question: On the matched firmware, does Delete Detector ID preserve the previous zone type or change it to Not Used?
gaps.reason: Configuration Guide page 22 first distinguishes preserving configuration from Default zone, but later says deletion sets the zone to Not Used. The conflicting statements are retained as a gap.
gaps.neededEvidence: Manufacturer clarification or controlled bench observation of the two distinct deletion commands; not a live protected detector.

gaps.title: Restricted-role and remote-password permissions
gaps.question: On the target firmware, can Guard, Set Only or Duress users reach Pair App, and can a Master user edit their own Remote Password?
gaps.reason: The table includes restricted roles for Pair App although the role descriptions say those roles lack user-menu access. The Remote Password row omits Master/Admin, while the editing prose describes personal remote-password editing more broadly. Normal-user output operation is explicitly supported by both the table and the role description.
gaps.neededEvidence: Screens from named role and firmware, or an updated manufacturer user guide.

gaps.title: Pendants is missing from the printed summary map
gaps.question: Where does Test→Pendants appear in the user menu on the target firmware?
gaps.reason: User-guide page 45 documents Test → Pendants, but the map on printed pages 28–29 omits it. The body establishes the route; the LCD position remains unverified.
gaps.neededEvidence: Video or ordered photographs scrolling the Test menu on the matching firmware.

gaps.title: Unenumerated dynamic and protocol details
gaps.question: Which exact communications-format values or installation-specific screens should be exercised next?
gaps.reason: The atlas maps documented menu routes and principal type selectors. It does not enumerate every protocol code, text-entry state, log message or conditional outcome.
gaps.neededEvidence: A specific menu/path and target firmware so the next behavior can be verified without guessing.

gaps.title: Calendar edit labels differ from creation prompts
gaps.question: On the target user firmware, does Edit Event display Ward/Partitions or Event Actions, and where is the exception selection?
gaps.reason: The 7.02.xx summary uses Ward/Partitions and omits exceptions, while the Add Event body uses Event Actions and Event Exceptions. The older installer guide uses Actions and Exceptions.
gaps.neededEvidence: Ordered photographs of Calendar Set → Edit Event and Edit Exception on the identified firmware.
